I need to write JUnit 4 tests for jsoup's Selector class, importing Document, Element, and Jsoup to parse real HTML for test cases—but I'm noticing the provided classpath doesn't seem to include the jsoup core jar, which would be a problem.

Actually, since this is Defects4J Jsoup-12b, the Selector class is source under test and should compile alongside the rest of jsoup's source (Element, Document, Jsoup, Elements), so it's already part of the project classpath rather than needing a separate jar—the jar list given is just extra dependency libraries like commons-lang, gson, jetty, and junit/hamcrest. I'll proceed writing tests that parse HTML with Jsoup.parse and run queries through doc.select or Selector.select.

Let me plan the coverage: testing Selector.select(String query, Element root) across tag/class/id/attribute/universal selectors, combinators, and pseudo-selectors like :lt, :gt, :eq, :has, :contains, :matches, :not, plus testing Selector.select(String query, Iterable<Element> roots) for multiple root elements.

I also need to verify that null or empty queries trigger IllegalArgumentException via Validate checks, malformed selectors throw SelectorParseException, combinators placed at the start of a query correctly anchor on the root, and edge cases like a top-level ":has(...)" selector are handled properly since the code adds all elements before processing the remainder in the parsing loop.

That confirms it actually calls has(), which consumes ":has" and the balanced parenthesis to filter parents containing descendants matching "p". I'm sketching a test HTML document with two divs—one containing paragraphs, one containing a span—to verify this branch, planning to use Jsoup.parse to build it, then mapping out each select() branch starting with leading combinator queries like ">p".

That resolves to just the direct p children of root. I also need to trace the ":has(" branch and the default path for tag/class/id/attribute selectors, plus how the while loop handles comma-separated groups and combinators like ">" versus a plain space between selectors.

For "div p" descendant case, seenWhite is true but the next char isn't a combinator, so it falls into the seenWhite branch using a space combinator, while "div p+p" or "div p~p" would hit adjacent/general sibling cases. The else branch covers AND selectors like "p.foo" where there's no whitespace, triggering intersectElements. Then I'm looking at the combinator switch statement handling '>', ' ', '+', '~', and considering how an invalid combinator character might trigger the default exception branch.

Now I'm mapping out the findElements() branches: byId for "#id" (both found and missing cases), byClass for ".class", byTag for matching tag names including namespaced ones like "ns|tag", and byAttribute selectors covering existence checks, prefix/suffix/contains/regex operators, plus an else branch that throws a SelectorParseException for unrecognized operators.

I'm noting that the attribute else-throw branch is effectively unreachable since consumeToAny already constrains the operator to one of the recognized tokens, so I'll flag it as dead code rather than test it directly. I still need to cover "*" for allElements, the ":lt(n)", ":gt(n)", ":eq(n)" index selectors, and ":has(...)" used within AND conditions like "div:has(p)".

Now I'm covering the remaining pseudo-selectors: ":contains", ":containsOwn", ":matches", ":matchesOwn", ":not", and verifying that an unrecognized token like "##" or ":bogus(" throws a SelectorParseException. I also need tests for consumeIndex rejecting non-numeric values inside ":eq(abc)", for select() with multiple root elements, and for Validate.notNull guarding against a null query.

I should also check that select() throws on null query, empty or whitespace-only query strings, and a null root element. The private filter helper methods (filterForChildren, filterForDescendants, filterForAdjacentSiblings, filterForGeneralSiblings, filterForParentsOfDescendants, filterForSelf, filterOut) are already exercised indirectly through combinator selectors like ":has", ":not", and sibling/child/descendant operators, so I don't need separate direct tests for those.

I'm also planning coverage for byId lookups both when an element is found and when it isn't, plus the byAttribute branches: attribute existence checks like "[href]", prefix-based checks like "[^data-]", and the various attribute value comparison operators. Since consumeToAny restricts which operators can be parsed, I can't directly trigger an invalid attribute operator path, so that edge case isn't testable this way.

I'm also thinking about namespaced tag names like "fb:name" -- Jsoup's lenient HTML parser should still create an element with that literal tag name even though it's unconventional, so I want to write a test that parses such a tag and queries it with "fb|name" to confirm the byTag logic handles the pipe-to-colon replacement correctly. Now I'm putting together the full test class structure, accessing the parsed Document's root and elements to run these assertions.

Writing JUnit test setup...

Now I'm adding tests for invalid inputs like null/empty/whitespace queries and null root throwing IllegalArgumentException, then starting basic matcher tests like selecting by tag name.

Adding more test cases...

Adding more attribute selector tests...

Adding more test cases...

Adding more test cases...

Adding more selector tests...

Adding more test cases...

I'm also verifying the expected element counts against the sample HTML structure to make sure the assertions match the actual document layout.

I'm also thinking about how Jsoup handles the namespaced tag like fb:name — since Jsoup normalizes tags to lowercase and HTML5 parsing allows colons in unknown tag names, this should parse fine as a single custom element.

Now I'm walking through expected sizes for each selector test: "p" should match the two paragraph elements under body, "#1" should find exactly one div by id, "#missing" should return zero results, ".outer" should match the two divs sharing that class, and "*" should match everything universally.

For the namespace tag test, "fb|name" gets converted into a "fb:name" tag lookup, and I'm checking whether jsoup preserves the colon in tag names during parsing rather than stripping it, since Tag.valueOf doesn't seem to validate against colons.

Moving through the attribute selectors: the exists check "[data-test]" only matches the first p (size 1), the prefix check "[^data-]" also only catches that same element, and "[class=foo]" does exact string matching against the class attribute, so it only matches the p with class="foo" precisely -- not the div/body with class="outer", and not treating class as multi-valued.

For "p[class!=foo]", I'm working through how the parser combines tag and attribute selectors without a space, which intersects as an AND -- first matching all p tags, then filtering by the not-equals attribute condition.

The second query finds elements where class isn't "foo", including elements with no class at all, then intersects with the p set. The p with class "foo" gets excluded, leaving only the p with class "bar" in the final result.

Working through more selectors now: prefix match "[class^=ou]" catches both divs starting with "outer", suffix match "[class$=ter]" also catches both divs since "outer" ends in "ter", and substring match "[class*=out]" similarly matches both divs containing "out". Each of these yields a result size of 2.

For the regex attribute selector matching digits, the divs with id="1" and id="2" match since they contain digit characters, but the span with id="only" doesn't, giving a size of 2 as expected -- I just need to make sure the regex is properly escaped as a Java string literal. Now I'm moving on to index-based selectors like "div:lt(2)" using the body as root.

For this selector, it first matches all div tags, then applies the ":lt(2)" pseudo-selector as an AND condition to filter by sibling index position, checking which elements have an index less than 2 among their siblings.

Intersecting the two div sets gives size 2, confirming the logic works. I'll keep the broader assertions (size>=1) for the trickier cases to avoid relying on exact counts I'm not fully certain of, while reasoning through the eq(0) case to double-check sibling-index intersection behaves as expected.

For the non-numeric index test, I expect Validate.isTrue to throw an IllegalArgumentException, which should satisfy that case. Now I'm thinking through the :has() selector's top-level behavior, starting from the full set of elements under root before applying the containment filter.

The query loop then re-enters processing on ":has(p)" from scratch, this time hitting the AND branch which invokes findElements() and matches the ":has(" prefix—consuming the token, extracting "p" as the subquery, and filtering the candidate set down to those parents containing a descendant p from that same broad element pool.

So the aggregated p elements get collected from within body and div1, then checking parents against those p tags should match body itself, div1, and possibly other ancestors depending on how far root.getAllElements() scopes -- since root is body, that scope stays within body's subtree, so the candidate parents end up being body, div1, and the p elements themselves plus any span.

For "div:has(p)" testing nested structure, I expect only div1 to be returned since it's the one directly containing a p element.

Tracing the query execution: the "div" token matches both div1 and div2 by tag, then the ":has(p)" subquery filters by checking which parents have p descendants. Since div1 contains p.foo and p.bar while div2 has none, the parent-child filtering should narrow the candidates down to just div1.

That intersection gives {div1}, matching the test's expectation. Moving through the remaining test cases: has() with empty subquery throws on validation, contains/containsOwn and matches/matchesOwn behave as expected with empty-string checks throwing, :not(p) correctly excludes p elements, :not() with empty argument throws, and now I'm checking the child combinator "div > p" case.

Starting with "div" matches by tag to get div1 and div2, then the loop checks for combinators - whitespace was consumed but the ">" character takes priority as a matched combinator, so it gets consumed and passed into the combinator handling logic.

Tracing through the ">" combinator: it consumes trailing whitespace, grabs "p" as the sub-query, then selects paragraphs within the div context and filters them to keep only those whose parent is directly one of the divs - landing on p.foo and p.bar as the final children matches.

Now I'm moving to the descendant combinator case "div p", starting with byTag matching for the divs before continuing through the whitespace-aware combinator loop.

For "p.foo + p" adjacent sibling selector, I need to trace how findElements parses the first token "p" via matchesWord and byTag, checking whether consumeElementSelector actually consumes the full "p.foo" or just "p".

Continuing with "p.foo + p": after consuming "p", I check for combinators and find none immediately, so it's an AND operation—parsing ".foo" pulls elements with class foo under root, giving {p.foo}, then I intersect that with the current set {p.foo,p.bar} by filtering for elements present in both, narrowing down to just p.foo.

Now for the remaining " + p", I detect whitespace then the '+' combinator, consuming it and parsing the adjacent subquery "p". For sibling combinators like '+' and '~', the selection runs against the whole root rather than the current element set, so I select all p elements under root to use as the comparison pool for filterForAdjacentSiblings.

Checking which candidates share a parent with elements in my current set and whose previous sibling matches, I find only p.bar qualifies since its immediate predecessor is p.foo, so the final result narrows to {p.bar}, giving size 1 — matching the expected assertion.

Next for "p.foo ~ span", I select p.foo as the base, then gather all span elements across both divs. Filtering for general siblings requires matching parents, so span_only in div2 gets excluded immediately while span_in_div1 stays in play for position comparison.

Then I check test 29 with the "> div" selector, which starts at the root body element and uses the child combinator to find direct div children, verifying filterForChildren correctly matches div1 and div2 since both have body as their immediate parent.

Next I'm tracing test 30 for the group selector "p, span", where findElements first grabs all p tags, then the loop detects the comma and processes the remaining subquery for span, accumulating results from both branches.

I'm weighing whether to assert the exact count of 4 or keep a safer lower-bound check with assertTrue(size>=3) to avoid fragility from subtle behavior differences. I'll go with the precise assertEquals(4, els.size()) since the calculation checks out.

Right, the Elements wrapper just converts the final LinkedHashSet into a list, so duplicates are already stripped, confirming the size-4 result. The standalone "p.foo" selector test should similarly resolve to a single match, size 1, and I expect the unknown token "$unknown" case to throw a SelectorParseException.

Two divs selected with "p" applied individually, giving 2 paragraphs total from div1 and none from div2, matching the expected count of 2. Then checking that empty query strings and null roots correctly throw IllegalArgumentException and null-pointer validation errors respectively in the iterable select overload. Now I'm verifying the "p[class!=foo]" attribute-not-equals selector matches as expected.

I should also confirm "[data-test]" attribute only appears on the first p, and that selector correctly excludes it when negated. For the namespace case, I need to check whether Jsoup's parser handles a tag like "fb:name" correctly, since HTML parsers can sometimes mishandle colons in tag names and split them unexpectedly.

The HTML tokenizer reads tag names until whitespace or '>', so the colon won't cause issues -- "fb:name" should parse literally as one tag name without triggering any namespace handling. I'll trust this is standard jsoup behavior, since jsoup's own test suite likely covers this exact namespace selector scenario. I also want to double check other assertions like "contains(Three)" are safe regardless of case sensitivity, and confirm I've imported the needed utility classes for lists.

For the null query edge case, I expect Selector.select(null, root) to throw an IllegalArgumentException from Validate.notNull inside the constructor, consistent with similar defects4j jsoup tests. Now I'm putting together the final test code with comments noting which branches (like the unreachable else-throw cases in combinator() and byAttribute()) can't be tested through the public API, plus a test confirming SelectorParseException is reachable and another covering "p[class]" selectors.

I'm settling on roughly 35 tests for solid coverage, then finalizing the class with proper imports—Document, Element, Elements, Jsoup—checking whether Selector needs an explicit import since the test class lives in the same org.jsoup.select package.

Actually a redundant same-package import is legal in Java, just unnecessary, not an error, so I'll include it as requested since it's harmless. Elements is already in the same package so no import needed there either. I'll also add a negative test case for when the attribute selector key doesn't match any recognized operator, verifying it throws a SelectorParseException.

Since consumeToAny stops precisely at one of those six exact sequences, the subsequent matchChomp calls are guaranteed to succeed, confirming the else branch truly can't trigger. I'll note in comments that both unreachable else-throw branches, in combinator() and byAttribute(), are structurally unreachable given valid input through the public API.
